A_general.implementation_language: NOT FOUND for the hosted server; related public CLI is TypeScript.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: NOT FOUND for the hosted server; related CLI uses @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.12.1.

other_official_servers: https://github.com/Airtable/airtable-mcp-cli is an official CLI client for the hosted server, not a separate MCP endpoint.
https://github.com/Airtable/skills is an official repository of agent skills and plugin configuration that can connect to the same hosted server.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Airtable says MCP is included with all Airtable plans at no additional charge. Calls count against standard Airtable API rate limits.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Free plan: no charge. Team: $20/user/month billed annually. Business: $45/user/month billed annually. Enterprise Scale: custom pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP itself has no added charge. Airtable plans are seat-based; Team and Business charges apply to users with edit permissions for at least one base. MCP usage and created records count toward existing API and base limits.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires an MCP-compatible client and Airtable authorization. OAuth can be scoped to selected bases, apps, and workspaces; PAT scopes can be limited. Organization administrators may need to allow-list the integration. Calls are subject to standard API limits; record creation is limited to 10 per request.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Airtable controls service and API limits; organization administrators control third-party integration allow-listing; users and their Airtable roles, granted OAuth selections, and PAT scopes determine access.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official reference distinguishes actions by their documented behavior, but publishes no readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint annotations. The 40 documented tools include reads and mutations. 2. Server-side gates documented: automations created or updated through MCP remain drafts until reviewed and turned on in Airtable; delete_automation only deletes an automation that is off; active automations must first be turned off in the UI. No general confirmation parameter or MCP elicitation is documented. 3. OAuth scopes and PAT scopes bound access; OAuth allows selecting bases, apps, and workspaces. Permissions mirror Airtable user access; roles and organization integration allow-lists apply. Admin approval of a manually registered OAuth app is documented. Token expiry/revocation details are not published; users can remove bases or delete the integration. 4. Documentation describes scoped read-only access through scopes only: data.records:read, schema.bases:read, data.recordComments:read, workspacesAndBases:read. No URL tool filter, read-only endpoint, region-specific endpoint, or sandbox mode is documented. 5. Access follows existing Airtable permissions, including interface-only visibility boundaries. No MCP-specific PII masking or secret redaction is documented. 6. Calls count against standard API rate limits; create_records_for_table is limited to 10 records per request. Specific hosted result truncation or MCP per-call charges are not documented. 7. Hosted tool input schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published; no operator argument override is documented. 8. Airtable describes agent activity in organization audit logs; third-party AI actions trace to the integration and its installer. Audit event coverage is plan-dependent and rolling out; MCP-specific telemetry and opt-out are not documented. 9. The official 40-tool list has no feedback, rating, report, survey, or vendor-review tool. 10. Tool descriptions include workflow instructions, including preferring get_create_automation_instructions before automation creation; documentation recommends discovery. These are agent-facing descriptions, not evidence of server-enforced behavior. Airtable skills are separately installed. 11. No cross-session server memory affecting outputs or tool availability is documented. 12. One hosted endpoint and one documented flat tool list; no proxy subservers or nested AI agents are documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or universal escape-hatch tool appears in the official tool list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Saves the draft configuration only — it is off until the user reviews and turns it on in the Airtable UI. Prefer calling get_create_automation_instructions first.
Automations that are on must be turned off in the Airtable UI first.
AI tools typically call this once per session before building an automation.
Use list_workspaces first to find the workspace ID where you want to create the base.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One hosted endpoint with a single documented tool list; no endpoint-specific subservers or dynamically loaded toolsets are documented.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference at https://airtable.com/developers/agents/mcp/tools names 40 tools and identifies the exact input endpoint. Airtable's support article describes capabilities but does not give a separate total. MartechDB reports 40; mcp.so's rendered description lists 26 across categories while its fetched tool list is unavailable; Gamut lists 9; mcp.tc says live tools are behind sign-in; Claude's connector listing gives no names. No catalogue-only actions were added. The reference does not publish input schemas, so parameters are NOT PUBLISHED. All 40 tools are listed in actions.json.

E_aggregated.token_method: No hosted initialize instructions or verbatim tool schemas are available. Related public code is a client, not the deployed server; tool definitions were not retrievable from the unauthenticated endpoint.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: MCP cannot turn on automations; turning them on requires review in the Airtable UI. MCP cannot create or edit automation Script actions, add Interface filters, or edit an existing Interface. Field type and select-choice changes are not supported by update_field. Only workspace owners or creators can create bases, and base-level creator permission alone is insufficient. Sources: https://support.airtable.com/articles/9897799762-using-the-airtable-mcp-server and https://airtable.com/developers/agents/mcp/tools

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions instruct agents to call get_create_automation_instructions before building, use list_automations/get_automation before updating, and use list_workspaces before creating a base. Airtable advises users to check permissions and trust connected AI tools. These recommendations are not documented as server-enforced checks.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Airtable says the server respects existing permissions: “you can only access data you normally have permission to view or modify.” It says automation drafts remain off until users review and turn them on in the UI. The vendor describes agent activity audit logging and attribution to the third-party integration and the person who set it up.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Airtable states MCP is available on all plans with no additional Airtable charge, supports MCP-compatible clients, and respects user permissions. The vendor also states users can remove specific bases or delete the integration to revoke access.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and scoped authorization are documented for the hosted service, as are draft-only automation changes and the inactive-automation deletion restriction. Audit logging is a vendor-documented organization feature with rollout and plan limits; MCP-specific logging details are not specified. Trust and permission-check advice is instructional text, not a documented server-side control.

contradictions: OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises data.recordComments:read and data.recordComments:write scopes, but the official 40-tool reference lists no comment-related tool. This may reflect scopes used elsewhere in the product or capability not described in the reference; the evidence does not resolve the difference.

Third-party listings expose partial subsets of the official list: Gamut names 9 tools, while MartechDB reports a 40-tool catalog. The official reference names all 40 and remains the action-list source.
observations_for_research: The published tool descriptions combine action names with agent-facing sequencing advice; the documentation does not establish that this advice is enforced by the server.
Airtable distributes agent skills separately from the MCP endpoint, and describes those skills as adding domain-specific knowledge for connected models.
Airtable says tool names, behaviors, and capabilities may change; the related CLI discovers the live catalog at runtime.
notes: Reviewed prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages and code folders, including page6.html and page6.script.txt for the official tool reference; found no official hosted tool schemas or initialize instructions. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 in the supplied evidence. The Airtable CLI and skills repositories were inspected; neither contains deployed server code.
